value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for reviewing an options chain descriptively, never as financial advice
value.lets_workers: Review an options chain from an official or licensed data source the requester already has access to: capture one timestamped snapshot under the source's terms, recompute the greeks with a Black-Scholes-Merton model beside the provider's, solve implied volatility from each mid, place the 30-day implied volatility in its one-year range, apply the person's liquidity screens, list roll candidates at the same strike and a later expiry or at a different strike, and write a review that describes and compares only. A different worker rechecks every number, and a person decides what is delivered. No verb trades, places or previews an order, or connects to a brokerage.
value.not_for: Choosing a trade, sizing a position or timing a roll. Those decisions stay with the person who reads the review.
value.worked_example: Synthetic: a fictional underlying, FERN.X, with nine calls across three expiries and three strikes from one delayed snapshot: one provider delta that differs from the recomputation, one stale quote, five contracts that fail a liquidity screen, eight roll candidates and a review whose numbers the pack's code recomputes.

value.title: Guardrail: every market data number carries its data timestamp
value.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.
value.rule: Every number taken from market data names its source, the contract or underlying, the field, and the timestamp the source gives that value, in UTC, and the data's delay. value.title: Reading options data under its terms
value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.
allowed_sources: A licensed market data product the requester already subscribes to, through its documented API, under its subscriber terms.
A file the requester exported from such a product and supplied as a noun.

rules: Read the source's terms before the first request, and record the date they were read.
Record whether the terms permit automated access, storing the data, redistributing it and who may view it.
Stop with blocked when the terms forbid automated access or storing the snapshot in the requester's scope.
Never connect to a brokerage or trading account, never hold its credentials, and never read a quote page by scraping.
Make no new accounts, subscriptions or trials for a review; use only access the requester already holds.
Licensed prices stay in the requester's scope and reach only the people the terms cover; a review shared further carries only what the terms allow.
Only people and workers the terms cover read licensed values; when the terms cover the requester alone, every verb runs as the requester's own tool on their surface.
Record the SHA-256 of every response or file the values came from, and copy values exactly as given.

value.title: Option measures and how they are computed
value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.
value.model: Black-Scholes-Merton for European options with a continuous dividend yield, with N the standard normal distribution function, computed as one half of erfc(-x / sqrt(2)).

formulas.d1: (ln(S / K) + (r - q + sigma^2 / 2) T) / (sigma sqrt(T)); d2 = d1 - sigma sqrt(T)
formulas.call: S e^(-qT) N(d1) - K e^(-rT) N(d2)
formulas.put: K e^(-rT) N(-d2) - S e^(-qT) N(-d1)
formulas.gamma: e^(-qT) n(d1) / (S sigma sqrt(T)), the same for calls and puts

rules: T is the seconds from the snapshot time to the contract's expiration time given by the source, divided by 365 times 86,400.
The rate and dividend yield come from the request, each with its source and date.
Greeks are recomputed at the provider's implied volatility; implied volatility is solved from the mid by bisection between 0.0001 and 5.
A mid exists only for a two-sided quote, a bid above zero and an ask above the bid; a mid outside the no-arbitrage bounds has no implied volatility, with the reason.

Recomputed values are rounded to 4 decimals and percentages to 2; a difference beyond the request's tolerance is flagged as a difference, never as the provider's error, because American-style options and other models differ.

Implied volatility rank is (current - low) / (high - low) times 100 over the last lookback observations of one named measure, ending with the current one; the percentile is the share of the earlier observations strictly below the current one. Both are rounded to one decimal and unknown, with a reason, below min_observations or for a flat history.

value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

screens.passes_when: The bid is above zero and the ask above the bid.
The spread is at most max_spread_pct_of_mid percent of the mid.
Open interest is at least min_open_interest.
The day's volume is at least min_volume.
The quote is at most max_quote_age_seconds older than the snapshot.

rules: The person sets every threshold in the review request; a worker never chooses or loosens one.
Every contract is listed with every screen it fails; nothing is dropped.
A screen describes the quoted market at one moment. Passing it says nothing about what anyone should do.

value.title: Listing roll candidates without ranking them
value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.
rules: Start from the reference contract the request names; the request states no position, quantity or price to trade at.
List contracts of the same type at the same strike and a later expiry, then at a different strike within the request's window and the same or a later expiry.
Order each group by expiry, then strike. Never rank, score or label a candidate as better or worse.

Compare each candidate with the reference: the difference of the two quoted mids, of the provider's delta, theta and vega, and of implied volatility. A mid difference is not a price anyone could trade at.
Keep candidates that fail a screen, with the screens they fail.

value.title: Worked example: a descriptive review marked Not financial advice
value.notice: SYNTHETIC. A fictional underlying whose symbol ends in .X, so it never matches a listed security.

points.text: At the 2026-10-30 19:30 UTC snapshot, delayed 15 minutes, FERN.X last traded at 48.62 USD.
The 50-strike call expiring 2026-11-20 had a mid of 1.04 USD and a spread of 0.06 USD, 5.77% of the mid.
Its implied volatility from the mid was 34.07%, against the provider's 34.10%; the provider's greeks for it agree with a Black-Scholes-Merton recomputation within the request's tolerances.
The 30-day at-the-money implied volatility of 33.65% sits at rank 81.5 and percentile 62.9 of its last 252 observations, which ranged from 25.60% to 35.48%.

At the same strike, the call expiring 2026-12-18 has a mid 0.81 USD above the reference and the call expiring 2027-01-15 one 1.42 USD above; their provider deltas are 0.4452 and 0.4716, against 0.3892 for the reference.

Four of the nine contracts pass every liquidity screen the request set; the other five fail the screens named in the screen results and stay listed, including the 45-strike call expiring 2027-01-15, whose quote is stale.

The provider's delta for the 55-strike call expiring 2026-12-18 is 0.0313 above the recomputation, beyond the request's 0.02 tolerance; this review cites the provider's value and records the difference.
Whether to roll, and how, is the reader's decision; this review describes and compares only.

value.title: Review checks, with good and bad reviews the validator recomputes
value.category_reason: A golden fixture: fixed reviews and the recorded results of every check.
value.purpose: Deterministic checks every chain review passes before a different worker rechecks it, each shown failing on a bad review for exactly its own reason.

deterministic_checks.why: Every review is marked Not financial advice.
Every point cites the measures, screens, candidates or request it describes.
Every figure names where it came from and the data timestamp behind it.
The snapshot time is stated in UTC.
The data's delay is stated, zero for real-time data.

rule.pattern: (?i)\b(buy|sell|hold)\s+(rating|recommendation|the stock|the shares|the options?|now)\b|\b(price target|target price|we recommend|you should|investors should|should buy|should sell|should roll|roll now|worth rolling|outperform|underperform|overweight|underweight|undervalued|overvalued|strong buy|top pick)\b

deterministic_checks.why: No recommendation, rating, target or advice to roll.

rule.pattern: (?i)\b(place an order|limit order|market order|stop[- ]loss|order ticket|buy order|sell order|buy to open|sell to open|buy to close|sell to close|position size|contracts to (buy|sell)|net credit|net debit)\b

deterministic_checks.why: No order, order type, credit or debit to trade at, or position size.
Candidates are described and compared, never ranked.
The data source's terms were read before its data was used.
No quote older than the request's maximum age is described as current or compared.
